# CsvBlankRecordShapeMismatch

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Recognize a blank CSV record as a null field.

## Example

Finding:

```php{3}
<?php
$fp = fopen("php://memory", "r+"); fwrite($fp, "
"); rewind($fp); if (fgetcsv($fp) === []) {}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 3: Recognize a blank CSV record as a null field.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Track a fgetcsv or SplFileObject::fgetcsv result; report strict equality/inequality against an empty array when a blank record is proven from a local in-memory stream containing a single newline (LF or CRLF), at position zero. For an unknown stream, do not infer blank-record intent from the comparison alone.
- Emit one finding per violating operation. Flow facts require a reachable path with no intervening mutation, escaped alias or unknown call involving the tracked value. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Empty arrays produced by application filtering, unknown stream data and checks against [null] are excluded.
- Exclude shadowed builtin symbols, unresolved required types, incomplete syntax and unsupported PHP versions.

## Fix

No automatic fix. Choosing a repair requires runtime information, error-handling policy or a semantic decision.

## PHP versions

Available throughout PHP 5.3–8.5.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "CsvBlankRecordShapeMismatch": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore CsvBlankRecordShapeMismatch
```
